items.summary: NANOROBOT-ENHANCED DIGITAL TWINS OF BRAIN STATE AT THE LIMIT A multiscale, uncertainty-aware research atlas on microrobotic observations, neural inverse problems, active model discrimination and the limits of computational brain twins. This research monograph asks whether additional microscale observations or strictly bounded reversible experiments can distinguish competing neural-state models that explain conventional measurements equally well. The twin is explicitly defined as a versioned scientific belief, not a digital person, a mind reader or a clinically validated instrument. Its objective is not maximum model complexity but improved identifiability, calibrated prediction under new conditions and faithful retention of failed hypotheses. The work develops five layers: multiscale neural and microenvironment state representation; posterior equivalence and prior sensitivity; non-clinical safe experimental design; frozen-version forking, rollback and reference ancestry; and blind prospective validation against classical state-space systems and independently specified alternatives. Its research architecture includes 30 distinct mathematical derivation plates linked to later chapters, 82 chapters with five independently paginated research sections apiece, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 revisable Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger identifies existing support for brain modeling, latent neural dynamics, experiment design and preclinical microrobot tracking while preventing those sources from being mistaken for evidence of the proposed integrated system. Key research questions include: Can two equally accurate virtual brains be separated by a small, permissible observation? How can the effect of a measurement itself be separated from neural change? When does a prior dominate the inferred brain state? Can the model predict unseen function rather than reconstruct a training signal? Can another laboratory reproduce a rejected twin and safely return to an earlier version? SCIENTIFIC STATUS AND LIMITATIONS This is a forward-looking, non-clinical research synthesis and experimental hypothesis architecture. It provides no personal medical advice, patient-specific interpretations or instruction to deliver neural interventions. Existing murine microrobot tracking and virtual-brain modeling studies do not establish autonomous neural nanorobot readout, human safety, privacy-sensitive mind inference or therapeutic efficacy. Proposed formulas, experiments, research gates and answer embryos are not newly validated biological laws or executed experiments. The work keeps independent safety vetoes, privacy, external reproducibility and explicit model retirement as first-class constraints. Research questions remain open to refutation, correction and reconstruction by future human and AI researchers.

items.summary: Fisher information metric tensors for the 41 held-out SONICOM test subjects, as used in “Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information” (D. Bassett). Code and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/domfrbassett/fisher-rao-hrtf-upsampling What the tensors are At each of the 793 directions of the SONICOM grid, the 2×2 tensor g = JᵀΣ⁻¹J describes how well the auditory cues separate that direction from its neighbours. J is the spatial Jacobian of the cues: Barumerli monaural PGE features, ILD and MaxIACCe-transformed ITD, each fitted with real spherical harmonics. Σ holds the cue noise (σ_mon = 1.25 dB, σ_ILD = 1 dB, σ_ITD = 0.569). All fields are low-pass filtered at 16 kHz before the cues are extracted. The tensor is expressed in a local tangent basis u₁ = a × r, u₂ = r × u₁, where a = z, or y when |r_z| > 0.9, and its units are d′² per rad². Contents metric_tensors.zip has one folder per subject, metric_tensors/subject_####/ , containing 25 files per subject (1,025 in total): reference_metric_tensor.mat : the dense measured HRTF. <METHOD>_N###_metric_tensor.mat : one file per reconstruction. There are six methods: SUpDEq_SH , SUpDEq_MCA , SUpDEq_NN_MCA_6dB (SUpDEq-Natural-MCA in the paper), SUpDEq_Bary_MCA_6dB , RANF and FSP_AE . Each is reconstructed from N = 100, 19, 5 and 3 retained directions. The 164 natural-neighbour and barycentric files at N = 5 and 3 have status “ not_applicable ”. The interpolation is undefined for those masks, so these files carry no tensors. Variables in each file: metricTensor : the tensors at SH order 6 [2×2×793]. familyGram : per-cue-family Gram matrices JᵀJ before noise weighting, at SH orders 4, 6 and 8 [2×2×793×3 families×3 orders]. They let you recompute the tensors with other noise values or SH orders. In reconstruction files only: crossFamilyGram : the unsymmetrised cross terms J_refᵀ J_recon, same layout as familyGram . airmByDirection : the pointwise AIRM discrepancy from the reference. Metadata: coordinates (Cartesian and azimuth/elevation in degrees), cue band, noise values (reference files only), status (“ completed ” or “ not_applicable ”) and, for not-applicable files, a message giving the reason. SHA256SUMS.txt lists a checksum for every file. Format and use The files are MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), so MATLAB, h5py or any HDF5 reader can open them. Note that h5py reverses MATLAB’s axis order. scripts/fisher_lib.py in the repository reads them and recomputes tensors, AIRM and thresholds from the Gram matrices. To rerun the analysis scripts, unzip into results/evaluation/ so the subject folders sit in results/evaluation/metric_tensors/ . Provenance Produced with run_evaluation("tensors") from the repository above. The values are numerically identical to the tensor files behind results/evaluation/full_evaluation_summary.csv ; this run additionally stores the cross terms. The tensors are derived from the SONICOM HRTF Dataset (Engel et al., J. Audio Eng. Soc. 71(5), 2023, doi:10.17743/jaes.2022.0066). The SONICOM HRTFs are released under the MIT licence. This work develops research begun for the author’s B.Sc. dissertation at Birmingham City University.

items.summary: This technical note documents a conditional mathematical correspondence between the static spatial kernel used in conventional electromagnetic potential theory and the fixed-source gravitational potential in Lisa Doumbouya’s Harmonic Physics programme. Under supplied three-dimensional Euclidean geometry, spherical symmetry and stated boundary conditions, the derivation gives the static Green function 1/(4πr). Applying the existing gravitational source normalization yields the potential −μ/r, whose radial derivative gives the inward acceleration −μ/r². The note distinguishes potential, field amplitude, intensity, acceleration and optical measurement conversion, keeping geometric normalization separate from the distance exponent. The optical phase-ruler results are reviewed alongside the GRACE-FO forward forecasts. Calibrated reconstruction using measured phase retained micrometre-scale agreement with processed microwave ranging, while some forward models produced much larger errors. These results do not establish exponential error growth or identify a unique physical cause. The correspondence uses established mathematics and remains conditional on the supplied geometry, source calibration and physical interpretation. It does not establish an electromagnetic mechanism of gravity or derive spatial geometry from foundational Phase. The note includes the analytical proof, assumptions, evidence boundaries and requirements for a subsequent physical test. No new experimental data are introduced.

It provides the numerical source data, analytical implementation, calibration inputs, and results used to prepare the final article. The work examines finite fibre–matrix transfer, thermally activated composite response, cohesive-law identification, and the compatibility of reported strengths with uncertain fibre orientation and tensile capacity. The deposit contains one final analysis snapshot. It includes the reference formulation and the baselines, thermal alternatives, and cohesive-law candidates examined in the article. These are parts of the reported scientific assessment, rather than separate manuscript versions. Superseded model results, development archives, manuscript drafts, and unrelated source files are excluded. Contents • data/ contains numerical representations of published response curves, reported group statistics, study metadata, fixed constituent and pullout calibrations, optimizer initialization values, and published experimental/finite-element comparison curves. Curve identifiers preserve the link to the source study and figure. These are processed publication-based data, rather than original instrument records. • model/ contains the executable analysis scripts. They fit the concrete and composite controls, evaluate reference responses and competing baselines, compare response curves on matched displacement grids, assess orientation and conditional envelopes, test capacity compatibility, verify the independent finite-transfer solver, and fit/test the nested cohesive laws. model/screen_capacity.py provides a command-line conditional strength screen. • model/fesma/ contains the reusable mechanics: the Fe-SMA backbone and bond-slip law, nonuniform pullout and work-quadrature solvers, concrete/cohesive section response, activation and two-ended bridging diagnostics, capacity-budget relations, analytical envelopes and inverse compatibility relations. items.summary: This paper offers a candidate descriptive model based on the author’s retrospective account of internal agent-like experience during a past period of social isolation, emotional distress and perceived high cognitive load. It is a non-clinical reconstruction, not a technique, treatment or recommendation. No contemporaneous physiological, behavioral or neuroimaging measurements were recorded. The Opposition–Load–Coupling vocabulary organizes reported phases of self-talk, opposition, felt load, perceived coupling, autonomy, boundary degradation and disengagement. These are reported experiences and interpretive constructs, not demonstrated causal mechanisms. Claimed benefits and harms are unmeasured first-person reports. The Shared Value Anchor is an untested candidate predictor, not an established stabilizer or necessary condition. The case does not establish whether value conflict preceded initial boundary degradation or distinguish the proposal from a simpler load-based account. The model is situated alongside dialogical-self, Internal Family Systems, predictive-processing, imaginary-companion, writer-agency and tulpa literature. Any incremental contribution lies in the proposed coupling vocabulary and separately testable value-anchor hypothesis, not in discovering internal multiplicity or proving a new mechanism. Safety: do not intentionally induce or replicate the conditions described. This is the author’s own past experience, published at the author’s direction; no formal ethics approval or exemption is claimed. Version 4 incorporates author-adopted revisions following advisory and changed-text checks, including prior-involved AI reviewers. Those checks are not independent peer review, clinical validation or evidence of effectiveness.

items.summary: SELF-CALIBRATING NANO-NEURAL INTERFACES AND REFERENCE LINEAGE AT THE LIMIT Built-In References × Drift Attribution × Independent Functional Requalification STARLI / Institute XXIII / Research Flagship 17 PUBLICATION DESCRIPTION When a long-running neural interface changes, is the cause the sensor, the surrounding tissue, or the decoder? An adaptive algorithm can restore predictive accuracy while obscuring the physical origin of its own correction. This book proposes a rigorous, falsifiable architecture for self-calibrating nano-neural interfaces that must retain the scientific history of every reference and every update. Its central axiom is that self-calibration does not imply self-certification: measurement claims, permission to change, electrode safety and functional benefit demand independent evidence. The first coupling is the existence of physically traceable internal references that can be challenged against electrically and temporally independent standards. The second is a source-aware drift-diagnostic process that distinguishes electronics gain, electrode-tissue transfer, tissue-like surrogate changes, changing source signals and model/feature drift, explicitly recording instances of nonidentifiability. The third is external functional requalification, which can reject an apparently successful update after hidden-domain testing, material or reference replacement, loss of selectivity, missing raw observations, or inability to reproduce the frozen predecessor. This research monograph is divided into seven causal layers and 82 chapters. Five major subsections of each chapter are assigned independent pages, yielding 410 separately paginated technical essays. Thirty gold mathematical derivations are linked from chapter-opening equations to discriminating experiments. The mathematics includes augmented state-space observability, nonlinear observation functions, source-separation Jacobians, Kalman innovations, impedance spectroscopy, covariance propagation, change-point statistics, conformal coverage, selective risk, hard-veto constrained update eligibility, reference-bridge covariance, exact rollback and cross-laboratory requalification. A displayed formula is a candidate analytical instrument with stated dimensions and assumptions, not a discovered biological law. Two hundred detailed Research Gates are preserved at the rear: 82 interrogate source identifiability, another 82 challenge independent physical and evidential hard vetoes, and 36 require third-party reconstruction of a frozen reference history. Thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos propose revisable architectures, beginning with the Neural Interface Calibration Passport. The Passport ties an interface's physical identity to the raw analog and digitized record, calibrated unit chain, hardware reference ancestors, model and feature checksums, reasons for changing any reference, failed updates, revoked permissions, blinded requalification and rollback. These are proposed evidence structures, not commercially validated devices. The DOI bibliography contains 18 unique external research records covering chronic intracortical signal instability, low-dimensional BCI stabilization, decoder adaptation, long-term electrode-tissue behavior, complex impedance metrology, electrochemical reference limits, neural interface materials and conformal uncertainty under covariate shift. Selected publisher and PubMed pages were consulted for source metadata. Their findings cannot establish efficacy of the new self-calibration architecture; source-specific claims and independent replication would be necessary.

Added region_mean(coefficients, dw1, dw2, sigma1, sigma2, mask, *, shift_correlation=None, ref_sigma=None) and region_contrast(coefficients, dw1, dw2, sigma1, sigma2, mask_a, mask_b, *, shift_correlation=None) , returning a RegionEstimate : the mean strain and density of a map region, or region A minus region B, with the error split into shift noise (averages down over pixels), calibration (from a two-mode CalibrationResult ; does not average down) and reference frequencies ( ref_sigma ; does not average down, and cancels exactly in a contrast). region_mean also tests whether the pixels agree within their error bars (chi-square with 2 (N - 1) degrees of freedom, the same in shift space and in (strain, density) space) and reports the pixel spread. Validated against the mean and per-pixel covariances of SeparationModel.invert , separation_with_calibration , finite differences of a re-solve, and seeded Monte Carlo over 400 trials that repeat the calibration, the map noise and the reference error (spread within 12 % of the reported error bars). Propagation as in JCGM 100:2008 (GUM), 5.2.2, Eq. (13). SeparationModel.invert(..., shift_correlation=None) : the correlation of the two shift errors (from a joint fit) enters the error bars through the full 2 x 2 shift covariance. Zero gives the old result bit for bit. On 400 repeats of two overlapping E' + A'1 peaks the density error bar without the correlation is 27 % above the actual spread; with it, it matches (tutorial 2). separation_with_calibration passes it through. White, Econometrica 48, 817 (1980), for spectra whose noise level changes along the axis, as shot noise does. Fitted values are unchanged. On 600 seeded Poisson spectra the center scatter is 1.7 times the default error bar and within 10 % of the new one; checked also against an independent finite-difference sandwich (relative 1e-5). items.summary: This working paper develops a relational Phase interpretation of black holes within the Harmonic Physics research programme, using general relativity, exact Kerr geometry and semiclassical black-hole thermodynamics as its physical baseline. It examines how phase organisation, temporal reference, observer accessibility and information persistence might relate to black-hole closure. Within the proposed framework, a phase-cycle is a closed relational structure that supports recurrence. Measured succession requires distinguishable relations and persistent records, while geometry and causal history are treated as observer-level reconstructions. The temporal-anchor hypothesis concerns a deeper terminal condition at which the parent domain loses the internally usable references needed to resolve further clocks and geometry. This proposed condition is kept distinct from the regular event horizon, across which local evolution continues. Observation is described through a joint observation relation among admitted source organisation, a physical channel and an observer-capable organisation. Source state, coupling and registered record retain separate roles; changes in accessibility may alter registration while the source organisation persists. The paper consolidates three bounded mathematical findings: exact Kerr ingoing and outgoing endpoints can have opposite trapped and anti-trapped orientations with the same mass and spin parameters; spherical source/exterior matching leaves the transition law undetermined; and a leading slow-rotation calculation permits the same sign of angular momentum in closing and opening configurations. These results establish compatibility within the stated geometric constructions. A physical transition mechanism remains to be derived. Black-to-white-hole models provide external theoretical comparisons. Return to the original exterior and the opening of a daughter phase are treated as distinct hypotheses, each requiring an appropriate causal structure, state map and conservation accounting. The remaining requirements include an invariant parent-relative terminal criterion, a physical Phase-to-boundary map, transition dynamics, information and entropy accounting, and a stable nonperturbative rotating completion. The paper remains a developing theoretical interpretation supported by standard-geometry comparisons and bounded symbolic checks. It does not establish a physical black-to-white transition, information recovery through evaporation or a daughter universe. items.summary: This dataset provides computational supplements, source code, finite-state component data, and independently checkable BFACF certificates for Makoto Ozawa, "Merge Trees of Length-Filtered Lattice Knot Spaces" (arXiv:2605.25322). The data concern self-avoiding polygons in the simple cubic lattice under standard BFACF moves and a lattice-length filtration. The earlier release documents the complete minimal-layer merge trees of $4_1$ (four components at length 30 merging at length 32) and $6_3$ (twelve components at length 40, two at length 42, and one at length 44). It also documents selected nonminimal trefoil components born at length 26; these selected births are not claimed to exhaust the full filtered graph. The frozen-unknot construction consists of a 64-edge Hamiltonian lattice unknot with no length-preserving or length-decreasing BFACF moves. An independently verified sequence of 25,436 BFACF moves reduces it to the elementary square with peak length 66. A two-edge block-splicing construction gives frozen unknots of length $64m$ for every integer $m\ge1$. New in the 19 October 2026 update: A minimal 24-edge trefoil is spliced to the 64-edge frozen unknot to produce an explicit 88-edge trefoil admitting no length-nonincreasing BFACF moves. The additional files supply the lattice direction words and coordinates, connected-sum construction, local-move verifier, and sampled checks for $m=1,2,3,4,8,16$. Repeating the frozen unknot block before the final trefoil splice gives frozen trefoils of length $64m+24$ for every $m\ge1$; reflection gives both chiralities. The results imply infinitely many nonminimal strong local-minimum births for the unknot and for both trefoil chiralities, within the standard BFACF filtration. The exact merge height 66 is established only for the 64-edge unknot. For longer frozen unknots and trefoils the proofs give lower bounds $H(P_m,U)\ge64m+2$ and $H(R_m,Q)\ge64m+26$, respectively; no exact merge heights or unbounded minimax excess are claimed. The construction is discrete and does not establish a positive barrier in continuous ropelength-filtered knot spaces or a universal result for arbitrary knot types. The archive retains earlier datasets and provenance information. Reproducibility instructions identify which outputs come from complete finite enumeration, certified BFACF paths, protected-port constructions, or limited computational checks.

items.summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.

This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.

items.summary: Version 2.0 is a substantive revision of version 1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19174862). It supersedes the earlier procedural interpretation and its exclusion of competing explanations. The revised title is Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc. Reproduced descriptive findings are retained; failed model comparisons and photographic uncertainties are reported explicitly. The earlier version remains available through the record version history. We examine whether reproducible structural observations on the Phaistos Disc support a procedural interpretation. A pinned numerical transcription contains 242 main-sign positions, including one unreadable position, 45 readable sign types, 61 divider-defined groups and 18 supplementary stroke annotations. Source review reconciles counting and numbering conventions while retaining unresolved photographic uncertainty. The 02-to-12 side contrast persists after exact-family collapse. Adding side to a fixed position-only pairing predictor improves held-family loss by 0.082738 nats, but its exact conditional tail of 0.075 fails the frozen support rule. A positional mixture fails to outperform a bigram baseline. A separate directional test of the proposed 07-to-27 recovery relationship fails, with a one-sided permutation tail of 0.884. Supplementary-stroke comparisons have insufficient controlled overlap for the specified exact test. The work documents organization and constrains specific interpretations without establishing procedural functions or phonetic values. Corpus, code, protocols, full results and uncertainty ledgers accompany the paper.

items.summary: Oscilloscope probe compensation kits circulate between teaching laboratories, yet the calibration status of a kit is rarely transferred with the same rigour as the instrument it serves. the present analysis treats cross-course calibration transfer as a metrological problem and evaluates, by round-robin design, how bandwidth attenuation in a probe kit propagates into measurement discrepancy bounds when the kit is moved between courses. The evaluation is a replication-based characterisation of the before-after-control-impact estimator under a declared variance structure (between-cluster SD = 6.0, residual SD = 4.5, intraclass correlation = 0.64), with power estimated across 2000 design cells at cluster counts of 8, 16, 24 and 32 and effect sizes of 3, 5 and 8 percentage points.54 clusters are required to detect a 5-percentage-point effect at 80% power, and that the minimum detectable effect falls steeply as cluster count rises from 8 to 32. A first-order attenuation model links probe bandwidth to the fractional amplitude error at the test frequency, and the round-robin design is shown to bound the transfer discrepancy that a receiving course can expect. The contribution is a design-level calibration-transfer protocol that makes the discrepancy bound explicit before a kit leaves its home course, rather than after a student records a suspect waveform.
tags: probe compensation; calibration transfer; round-robin evaluation; bandwidth attenuation; measurement

items.summary: Version 1.6 adds four preregistered analyses of LEGA-C star-forming discs at z ~ 0.8 and of SPARC: KCAL, a calibration of the gas pressure coefficient against stellar JAM masses; PIPE-6, a0 at R_e and 2R_e from ionized gas; PIPE-7, a local SPARC control; and PIPE-8, JAM-gas offsets and a0 at both radii. It also adds two analyses that were designed but not run (PIPE-5, GAP). Combined reading: in the same galaxies the gas a0 rises outward (+0.30 dex on 40), the JAM a0 does not (−0.08, no pre-stated reading), and the JAM-gas mass offset falls outward (−0.16). With measured mass models local discs show no rise; with the LEGA-C stellar recipe the 53 massive discs show none, but all 138 rise by +0.14. Preregistrations and code were drafted with Claude (Anthropic) and audited by fresh Claude sessions; locks are self-recorded SHA-256 manifests with UTC times. See README_v1.6.md for contents, provenance, hashes and every post-score edit.   Version 1.5 adds a synthesis note, "What the a0(z) tests say together: a falling g_obs/g_bar where the errors allow a test, and a fitted scale set by the baryonic and pressure inputs at R_e" (a0z_synthesis_note.pdf; scripts, outputs, figures, searches and audits in a0z_v1.5_SYNTHESIS.zip). It is exploratory and post hoc: it was designed after every result in the record was known, it is not preregistered, and it changes no scored label. It uses the record's frozen PIPE-2 and PIPE-3 code unchanged as a library. What it finds: - Shape. LEGA-C (147 galaxies), the one sample whose errors allow a shape test, prefers a ratio g_obs/g_bar that falls with g_bar (PIPE-3's R; classical margin 12, about one jackknife standard error above the threshold of 4) across gas multipliers 0-2, pressure multipliers 0.5-2 and stellar shifts -0.2 to +0.1 dex. MSA-3D's flat trend (18 galaxies) does not reappear. - Scale. No sample measures a0. At LEGA-C's accelerations the fitted a0 responds about three times as fast as the baryonic mass at R_e: locally d ln a0/d ln M* = -2.2, d ln a0/d ln M_gas = -0.6, d ln a0/d ln k_press = +0.8, explained by the interpolation function's leverage (L = 2.96). Shifts of +/-0.1 dex in stellar mass span a0 = 0.78-2.25. A universal a0 = 1.2 and an evolving a0 = 2.2 differ by about 0.13 dex in stellar mass, or a factor of four in inner gas. Every record value except MSA-3D's lies inside the ranges these inputs produce. - Matched in stellar mass, LEGA-C, KROSS and RC100 have median offsets from one RAR that are not distinguishable, although direct fits in the window differ. No dependence of a0 on stellar mass is detected inside any sample. - Reading: the record does not require an evolving a0; a0 at z ~ 1 cannot be read off until the baryonic mass at R_e is known to a few hundredths of a dex. - Can it be tested now? Searches (identifiers and counts only) found almost no CO or dust detections in the high-a0 samples (MSA-3D 0 of 23; MUSE-DARK 6 of its 126-galaxy parent). For the nine RC100 galaxies with PHIBSS CO, a preregistered test would decide with probability 0.07-0.13 (PIPE4_FEASIBILITY.md), so no test was run. Audits: three independent fresh-session audits. Round 1: 1 BLOCKER (the draft attributed the scale to cold gas; the stellar masses are the stronger lever), 7 MAJOR; round 2: 1 MAJOR (Table I's SPARC row); round 3: 0 BLOCKER, 0 MAJOR, 3 MINOR, all fixed. items.summary: This computational package accompanies the Neuro-Symbolic MAPE-K governance testbed for agentic retrieval-augmented generation at the edge. It provides Python source, experimental inputs, measured outputs, provenance manifests, analysis tables, figures and readable evidence reports for two related campaigns: the October 2026 MAPE-K controller campaign and the separate 18 October 2026 dense-retriever control campaign. The retriever control records 3,744 retrieval trials and 640 clean-validation query evaluations across sparse, pretrained dense and clean-fitted dense retrievers. It performs no new generator or controller evaluation. The package preserves campaign-specific directory layouts and historical execution records. A dependency-light deterministic template smoke test supports inspection without language-model downloads or CUDA. Full inference and fitting used NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX 8 GB and platform-specific CUDA/PyTorch environments. Original host paths and observed package inventories are provenance records, not a universal portable lockfile; full main-campaign model weights are referenced by revision and checksum, while the retriever campaign includes its pretrained and clean-fitted checkpoints. A release verifier checks the curated file manifest and metadata. The original retrieval verifier also requires original source paths for its final host-specific integrity checks. Original project software is MIT licensed (SPDX: MIT), with collective copyright held by the MAPE-K contributors. Third-party terms remain applicable: O*NET 31.0 and UCI Adult-derived data and fixtures are CC BY 4.0 with attribution and modification notices; MiniLM model material and its clean-fitted derivative are Apache-2.0; BGE model material and its clean-fitted derivative are MIT with upstream attribution. File-specific notices, exact model revisions and checksums are retained. Experimental counts reuse base profiles and should not be interpreted as independent efficacy replications. The evidence does not establish population fairness, human-validated answer-quality superiority, or a guarantee of safe retrieved evidence.

items.summary: Machine-readable evidence and analysis code for a PRISMA-2020 systematic review of fairness in histopathology AI. Contents. (i) The dual-coded, adjudicated extraction table for the 88-study analytical corpus (61 from the main search, 17 from the demographic-term update, 2 retrieved in October 2026, 2 suggested in peer review, 1 candidate resolved on full text and 5 from a re-screen of the keyword-filtered records; 89 records, one conference abstract linked to its journal paper; the earlier 62- and 79-study tables are kept alongside), with the pre-pass snapshots and the script that applies the October 2026 revisions, with the raw multi-coder outputs and inter-coder agreement statistics; (ii) the screening, de-duplication and post-hoc eligibility-audit logs; (iii) adjudicated QUADAS-2 risk-of-bias judgements for all 88 studies, with per-coder judgements for the original 62; (iv) the full consensus-endorsement coding pipeline — screened review pools, the pre-specified random sample (n=30, seed 20260913), the coding specification, two independent coder passes, disagreements and their adjudication, and tallies with Wilson 95% confidence intervals; (v) the 39-dataset demographic-metadata audit; and (vi) a claim-by-claim statistics register mapping every reported number to its source rows, together with the code that produces each value. Full texts of the reviewed papers are not included, for copyright reasons. Code is licensed MIT; data tables are licensed CC BY 4.0. A SHA-256 manifest ( MANIFEST.sha256 ) covers every file in the package. This package is a working-tree snapshot of the manuscript as of 18 October 2026 (61 pp main + 45 pp supplementary).
